title: Illumination of Scripture
definition: The illumination of Scripture is the gracious work of the Holy Spirit by which He helps believers understand, receive, love, and rightly respond to God's written Word.
summary: Because sin darkens the mind and heart, believers need the Holy Spirit's help when reading Scripture. Illumination does not create new Scripture, but enables God's people to understand and embrace the Word already given.
christFocus: The Spirit illuminates Scripture to glorify Christ. He opens hearts to see the truth of the Gospel, the beauty of the Savior, and the faithful path of discipleship.

studySections.heading: The Need for Illumination
studySections.content: A person can read the words of Scripture and still miss the truth because the heart is dull, proud, fearful, or resistant. The Spirit gives light so the Word is understood and received.

studySections.heading: Illumination Is Not New Revelation
studySections.content: The Spirit does not replace Scripture or add a competing message. He helps believers understand, trust, and apply the written Word of God.

studySections.heading: Prayerful Dependence
studySections.content: Believers should ask God to open their eyes, humble their hearts, and give wisdom as they study Scripture.

studySections.heading: Illumination and Christ
studySections.content: The Spirit glorifies Christ by helping believers see the Gospel, trust the Savior, and walk in the truth revealed in Scripture.

sources: Scripture references listed in this doctrine entry.
